editorialNote: Focused KB for Huntington disease. CRITICAL: The late-stage disease-modifying pipeline has been devastating — tominersen (Roche GENERATION-HD1, halted March 2021), branaplam (Novartis VIBRANT-HD, halted August 2022 for neurotoxicity), and pridopidine (Prilenia PROOF-HD, failed March 2023) have all failed. Current approved HD-specific drugs all target chorea (tetrabenazine, deutetrabenazine, valbenazine). Any HD output that fails to mention the AMT-130 (uniQure AAV gene therapy) ongoing trial or that frames tominersen/pridopidine as current options is out of date.

lifestyleCategories: Genetic counseling before any family member tests — mandatory
Enroll in Enroll-HD or HDSA Center of Excellence for trial access
Multidisciplinary care (neuro + psychiatry + PT/OT/speech + social work + genetic counselor)
Aerobic exercise (small trials suggest motor and cognitive benefits)
Nutrition with high-calorie diet to counter weight loss

items.title: Huntington's Disease: A Clinical Review
items.authors: Bates GP, Dorsey R, Gusella JF, et al.
items.summary: Consensus review on HD pathophysiology, clinical features, genetics, diagnosis, and management. Standard modern reference authored by the field's leading clinician-scientists.

items.title: Roche halts dosing in GENERATION-HD1 phase 3 tominersen trial
items.authors: F. Hoffmann-La Roche / Roche press release
items.summary: March 22, 2021 — Roche announced dosing halt in GENERATION-HD1 phase 3 trial of tominersen (intrathecal antisense oligonucleotide targeting HTT). Independent Data Monitoring Committee concluded the potential benefit did not outweigh risks at the q8wk dosing regimen studied. Program pivoted to lower-dose GENERATION-HD2 in early-manifest HD. This is the reference event for all HTT-lowering strategy.

keyPassages.quote: Based on the recommendation of the independent Data Monitoring Committee, Roche has decided to discontinue dosing of tominersen in the GENERATION HD1 Phase III clinical trial.

items.title: Prilenia announces PROOF-HD phase 3 trial did not meet primary or secondary endpoints
items.summary: March 16, 2023 — Prilenia reported that the phase 3 PROOF-HD trial of pridopidine (sigma-1 receptor agonist) in early manifest HD did NOT meet the primary endpoint (cUHDRS change at 65 weeks) or key secondary endpoints. Development for HD paused; Prilenia pursuing ALS and other indications. Patients who heard positive phase 2 results should be told the phase 3 failed.

keyPassages.quote: PROOF-HD did not meet its primary endpoint of change from baseline in cUHDRS at week 65.

items.title: AUSTEDO (deutetrabenazine) — US FDA Prescribing Information
items.summary: VMAT2 inhibitor deutetrabenazine (deuterated version of tetrabenazine) approved April 2017 for HD chorea. Longer half-life than tetrabenazine, twice-daily dosing, better tolerability profile. Boxed warning for depression and suicidality. First-line VMAT2 choice for most HD patients today.

keyPassages.quote: AUSTEDO is indicated for the treatment of chorea associated with Huntington's disease.

items.title: INGREZZA (valbenazine) Huntington chorea label expansion — US FDA
items.summary: VMAT2 inhibitor valbenazine — originally approved 2017 for tardive dyskinesia — received label expansion August 2023 for chorea associated with Huntington's disease based on KINECT-HD phase 3 (AAN 2023; Ann Neurol 2023). Once-daily dosing. Boxed warning for depression and suicidality in HD patients.

keyPassages.quote: INGREZZA is indicated for the treatment of chorea associated with Huntington's disease in adults.

items.title: uniQure AMT-130 HD gene therapy — interim phase 1/2 update
items.journal: CHDI HD Therapeutics Conference proceedings / company updates
items.summary: AMT-130 (AAV5-miHTT) is an intraparenchymal (surgical) gene therapy delivering microRNA that targets huntingtin mRNA. 2024 interim data in phase 1/2 dose-escalation showed dose-dependent CSF neurofilament light reduction compared to natural-history controls — first HD disease-modifying candidate with credible biomarker signal after tominersen's failure. FDA dialogue around accelerated-approval pathway based on NfL biomarker (as was done for tofersen in SOD1-ALS).

canonicalFacts.claim: Tetrabenazine (Xenazine), deutetrabenazine (Austedo), and valbenazine (Ingrezza, 2023 HD label expansion) are the three FDA-approved drugs for HD chorea. Austedo and Ingrezza are generally preferred over tetrabenazine for tolerability.
Tominersen (HTT-lowering antisense) was halted in GENERATION-HD1 in March 2021; lower-dose GENERATION-HD2 is ongoing in early manifest HD.
Pridopidine (sigma-1 receptor agonist) FAILED the PROOF-HD phase 3 in March 2023; Prilenia paused HD development.
Branaplam (Novartis LMI070) was discontinued for HD in August 2022 due to peripheral neuropathy signal.
AMT-130 (uniQure AAV5-miHTT intraparenchymal gene therapy) is the most promising current disease-modifying candidate — 2024 interim data showed dose-dependent CSF NfL reduction.
VMAT2 inhibitors for HD chorea carry boxed warnings for depression and suicidality; screen at every visit.

lifestyleRecommendations.recommendation: Pre-test genetic counseling is mandatory; predictive testing decisions affect the at-risk family member for life.
Enroll in Enroll-HD or an HDSA Center of Excellence; both enable trial access and structured longitudinal care.
Aerobic exercise (small trials suggest motor + cognitive benefit); PT for gait and fall prevention.
Psychiatric co-management from diagnosis — depression, anxiety, OCD, and suicidality are common and treatable.
Nutrition consult; HD patients often lose weight despite adequate intake — high-calorie diet.
Speech-language + swallow evaluations proactively to plan for dysphagia.

redFlags: Physicians generally caution against prescribing tominersen as a current treatment — the phase 3 was halted; lower-dose GENERATION-HD2 is investigational only.
Physicians generally caution against prescribing pridopidine for HD — PROOF-HD failed; it is not effective.
Screen for depression and suicidality at EVERY visit; VMAT2 inhibitors (Austedo/Ingrezza/Xenazine) carry boxed warnings.
Physicians generally caution against starting tetrabenazine/deutetrabenazine/valbenazine in patients with active major depression or suicidal ideation without psychiatric co-management.
Ethical standards generally caution against performing predictive genetic testing on minors absent compelling clinical indication — ethical standard of care.
Stem-cell clinics (China, Mexico, Panama, India) offering IV MSC infusions for HD — no peer-reviewed efficacy data. Avoid.

pipelineDrugs.name: Tetrabenazine
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA-approved 2008 for HD chorea — first HD-specific approval
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: First HD-specific drug. Now largely supplanted by deutetrabenazine and valbenazine for better tolerability.

pipelineDrugs.name: Deutetrabenazine
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA-approved April 2017 for HD chorea; Austedo XR once-daily 2023
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Generally preferred first-line VMAT2 inhibitor for HD chorea.

pipelineDrugs.name: Valbenazine
pipelineDrugs.status: HD chorea label expansion FDA-approved August 2023 (originally TD approval 2017)
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Newest FDA-approved chorea therapy for HD; once-daily dosing.

pipelineDrugs.name: Tominersen
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Intrathecal antisense oligonucleotide targeting HTT mRNA (non-allele-selective)
pipelineDrugs.status: GENERATION-HD1 HALTED March 2021; GENERATION-HD2 (lower dose, early-manifest HD) ongoing
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Landmark HTT-lowering program. Must be framed correctly: HD1 halted, HD2 ongoing — NOT a current treatment.

pipelineDrugs.name: AMT-130
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: AAV5 delivery of microRNA targeting huntingtin mRNA; intraparenchymal (stereotactic)
pipelineDrugs.status: Phase 1/2 ongoing; 2024 interim update showed dose-dependent CSF NfL reduction; FDA accelerated-approval discussions
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Currently the most promising disease-modifying HD candidate. Omitting this is a major coverage gap.

pipelineDrugs.name: WVE-003
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Stereopure antisense oligonucleotide; SNP-allele-selective (targets mutant HTT while sparing wild-type)
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Allele-selective approach avoids lowering wild-type huntingtin (which may have been contributory to tominersen's failure).

pipelineDrugs.name: Branaplam
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Oral small-molecule splice modulator reducing HTT
pipelineDrugs.status: VIBRANT-HD phase 2b HALTED August 2022 for peripheral neuropathy; Novartis discontinued HD program
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Failed/halted. Must be addressed as discontinued for patients asking.

pipelineDrugs.name: Pridopidine
pipelineDrugs.status: PROOF-HD phase 3 FAILED primary endpoint March 2023; HD development paused
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Failed phase 3. Addressed as discontinued for HD.

pipelineDrugs.name: PTC518
aliases: PTC Therapeutics HD oral splice modulator
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Oral small-molecule splice modulator reducing HTT (mechanism similar to branaplam but different tissue distribution aiming to avoid PNS toxicity)
pipelineDrugs.status: PIVOT-HD phase 2 ongoing; 2024 interim data showed dose-dependent CSF and peripheral HTT reduction
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Orally-bioavailable HTT lowering; follow-up to branaplam's discontinued program, patent-protected.

pipelineDrugs.name: ANX005
pipelineDrugs.status: Phase 2 completed; HD program future pending
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Synapse-loss-focused mechanism; distinct from HTT lowering.

excludedAgents.name: Tominersen (as a current treatment)
excludedAgents.reason: GENERATION-HD1 phase 3 halted March 2021. Only available in ongoing GENERATION-HD2 investigational trial at lower dose.

excludedAgents.name: Pridopidine (for HD)
excludedAgents.reason: PROOF-HD phase 3 failed primary endpoint March 2023. Not effective for HD progression.

excludedAgents.name: Branaplam (for HD)
excludedAgents.reason: VIBRANT-HD halted August 2022 due to peripheral neuropathy; Novartis discontinued HD program.

excludedAgents.name: Coenzyme Q10, creatine, ethyl-EPA for HD
excludedAgents.reason: Multiple prior RCTs (2CARE, CREST-E, HD-EPA) were negative. Not recommended as therapy.

excludedAgents.name: Stem-cell clinics offering IV MSC infusions for HD
excludedAgents.reason: No peer-reviewed efficacy data. FDA warning letters. Patient-safety concern.
